# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 preserved behavior and passed simulation, timing, and metric gates, but the parallel CRC equations synthesized to the same 16 LUTs and 34 FFs as the incumbent, so it failed the strict `minimize_luts` objective. The design is already timing-feasible at WNS 0.445 ns and WHS 0.208 ns; the next trial should target stored state while retaining the known top latency annotation `// @latency 1`.

## Hypothesis

Deriving the running CRC from the registered output CRC and `out_last_reg` can remove the separate 16-bit `frame_crc` bank, reducing FF use and potentially reducing LUTs if the frame-seed selection folds into the CRC logic.

## Instruction for generator

In `crc16_stream_core`, remove `frame_crc` and derive the CRC update state from `out_crc_reg` when the previous accepted byte was not last, or `16'hFFFF` when `out_last_reg` is set. Set `out_last_reg` to 1 on synchronous reset as the initial-frame marker; output payload and `out_last` are unspecified while `out_valid` is low. Keep the output CRC and last registers stable during stalls, preserve the one-slot ready/valid logic and reset priority, and retain the top’s `// @latency 1` annotation. The candidate is useful only if routed LUTs decrease, or LUTs stay equal and FFs decrease, while all verification and timing gates pass.
